subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default proactive retention policy for stale session archive artifacts beyond the existing deleted/reset retention, store-temp cleanup, unreferenced-artifact sweep, and disk-budget paths?
rationale: Current source shows real partial cleanup, but broad automatic deletion of session archives affects retention, diagnostics, and recovery semantics, and an open PR already covers the narrower deleted/reset reporting gap.

options.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
options.body: Define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts are automatically removed, under which retention and cleanup-mode rules.

options.title: Land Narrow Reporting First
options.body: Treat the open linked PR as the immediate deleted/reset visibility fix and defer broader `.bak.*` and proactive cleanup until more production evidence lands.

options.title: Split By Artifact Class
options.body: Keep this broad report as a parent and route each remaining suffix or sidecar class to a narrower canonical issue with its own safety proof.

recommendation.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts are automatically removed, under which retention and cleanup-mode rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup UX and maintenance controls that the broad cleanup policy would extend at the command/operator boundary.
